# The grammar of English (K2): why the words sit where they sit. One pattern per
# line as 'name: places', each byte as two hex digits (scripts/hex.sh). A place is
# a category (a space written as '_': auxiliary_verb, proper_noun), the role of
# that place after '/' (subject, predicate, attribute, object, complement,
# modifier, link, none), and a mark after that: '?' for an optional place, '*'
# for any number, '+' for one or more. 'a|b' is one place that takes either; to
# choose between sequences, group each: '((a b)|(c d))'. '(...)' groups places
# and takes a role and a mark of its own; a place without a role takes the role
# of its group. A line '@name = places' defines a group to use as '@name' in
# later lines. The first pattern that fits a sentence gives the roles of its
# words; a place takes fewer words first, so the shortest reading wins.
# Validated conceptions add their own patterns at run time (larry grammar).
